Then remarkable runs by Tony Verdie and Tony Stone on legs two and three brought the Belgrave team up to 2nd place just two seconds from the lead.
Tony Verdie had been suffering from a series of injuries but was back to form with 19th place in the Flying Fox Marathon and a time of 2 hours 51 mins 18 secs.
Perhaps the best Belgrave performances were by 2nd claim member Jim Estell who ran 2:25.31 and 54 year old Tony Verdie, in such good form at present and who ran 2:50.51.

Tony Verdie runs his fastest marathon since 1986 Tony Verdie overcame injury problems to his ankles and calf muscles, and a nasty stomach virus which limited him to an average of only 44 miles per week in the eight weeks leading up to the race, to run a fine M50 2:48 in the Dublin Marathon on the same day.
Perhaps the best performances were from the pair of over 50's in the quartet - Tony Verdie, who ran 16:34 on the first leg, and Tony Stone, not much slower on the second leg in 17:02.

Again it was windy, but times were about the same as last year with Tony Verdie running very well for fourth fastest on the day. Bill Laws, after his recent spell of warm weather training, ran quicker than a year ago and Tony Stone was only marginally slower despite running a 10km on the morning of the relay.

Another good run came from Tony Verdie in M50 section of the Tadworth '10' road race on December 29th. His 57:34 gave hime 3rd place behind Blackheath's O'Gorman, 56:51, and North London's Tom Ryan, 57:09.

Tony Verdie comfortably took the V55 race with his 79:33; his time was faster than any of the V45s. Jim Ryle's 71:57 in the Swanley Half-Marathon on March 23rd gave him 7th place just over a minute outside the place medals.

The M50 team had to scratch from the National Vets' six stage relay in Manchester at the last moment, even though we had Tony Verdie and Laurie O'Hara, and we were similarly unable to field a team in the South of England 4-stage relay at Aldershot.

Two Belgravians finished well up in the M50 age group - Tony Verdie was 2nd (42nd overall) in 28:13 and Tony Stone was 5th in 29:51. The "Dysart Dash" at Richmond saw Tony Stone take the M50 prize home after touring the 10k course in 37:04.
Tony Whatley, an old friend of Tony Verdie's from some way back, turned out for the Belgrave Half-Marathon, hoping to renew their acquaintanceship.
Best run of the day was again from Tony Verdie who seems to like this event. He completed the second fastest lap in 13:51 to Davidson's 13:39.

Tony Verdie, who is actually an M55, won the M50 section of the race in 58:20. Interestingly, an age-graded system was also used at this event and when the age weighting had been applied to all competitors in the race Tony came out as 4th best on the day, just ahead of the actual winner who clocked 49:57.
Tony Verdie was placed 2nd in the age graded result.
